claims.text: The material family is face-centered-cubic Fe-Co-Ni-based high-entropy alloys.
The targeted property is saturation magnetization.
Optimizing local chemical disorder can significantly enhance saturation magnetization by maximizing the orbital magnetic moment contribution.
Strong thermal spin fluctuations suppress the orbital magnetic moment in the equiatomic Cantor alloy.
The itinerant-electron character of the equiatomic Cantor alloy contributes to suppression of its orbital magnetic moment.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is a chemically disordered FCC solid solution at ambient pressure.
Non-equiatomic ratios, Zr or Al additions, or Co-rich variants can modify the local electronic environment.
The proposed compositional changes can reduce thermal spin fluctuations without inducing secondary-phase precipitation.
A single-phase FCC CoCrFeMnNi solid solution can be maintained under suitable compositional and microstructural control.
Local chemical short-range order modifies the d-band electronic density of states.
The modified d-band density of states influences spin-orbit coupling strength.
High configurational entropy and chemical disorder generate thermal spin fluctuations that quench the orbital magnetic moment.
Composition tuning can reduce spin fluctuations or enhance spin-orbit coupling through selected local atomic environments.
Increasing the orbital-moment contribution will increase the total saturation magnetization.
The intervention will increase both saturation magnetization and the orbital-to-spin magnetic-moment ratio relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
FCC CoCrFeMnNi has high ductility and fracture resistance or toughness, particularly under cryogenic conditions.
The modified alloys can retain the ductility and fracture toughness of the FCC baseline while their magnetic properties improve.
Formation of BCC, sigma, or other brittle secondary phases would degrade ductility or toughness.
The cited evidence does not quantify the orbital-moment contribution or establish its proposed suppression mechanism in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
XMCD can be used to extract spin and orbital magnetic moments for the proposed comparison.
